ctx.x: Bud, as I say, let us go right back to the beginning, and you tell me everything that you can think of about early days because we've got lots of time and we should hear all we can about that.

Well, I think that I was conscious of music at the age of eight, because first of all, my mother is a pianist and she had five sisters and two brothers, all of whom played the piano, and they were constantly visiting us, because we had this lovely old upright, a Kimball piano. One of the best of its kind, in those days, at least.

So, again, I was aware of music because that was all I heard. And then my father had -- he was not musically inclined but he loved it -- and he had in those days, the Victrola put out this big high standup player, record player, called the -- similar to the Victrola, and they gave a lot of operatic records. We had all of Caruso, they gave us symphonic records, they gave the old Paul Whiteman, Isham Jones records, you know, those were the big dance bands of the day, and I was constantly playing these things, you…
